synopsis: VAMPO post-trains a video predictor with rewards for agreement with expert future latents, then trains a separate action policy on its predictive features. First-step stochastic denoising concentrates optimization where the action policy obtains its representation. The supplied v1 reports stronger simulated manipulation and higher real-robot task scores, but latent agreement does not directly measure contact accuracy or guarantee control success.

problem.text: The authors argue that likelihood-surrogate video training can produce plausible futures with small pose, spatial-relation or contact-timing errors that mislead manipulation. VAMPO targets this mismatch between prediction and control. Its reward still measures latent consistency with demonstrations, rather than executed task return.

contributions.text: Recast video denoising as a decision process and post-train the existing VPP predictor without introducing a new control architecture.
Combine a first-step Euler-Ancestral transition, deterministic completion, and group-relative policy optimization using non-adversarial latent rewards.
Test representation transfer with an unchanged action model and a subsequently trained action model, alongside longer-horizon and real-robot evaluations.

inputs: Current observation o and language instruction l
Training only: expert future clip N and demonstrated action sequence a
outputs: Predicted future latent and first-denoising-step feature h-hat
Separate AGM prediction of an executable action sequence

steps.name: Predict in latent space
steps.detail: A Stable Video Diffusion VPM conditions on observation and instruction. A pretrained VAE encodes the expert future clip as the clean target. Initial supervised training reconstructs clean video latents from noisy inputs.

steps.name: Define denoising actions
steps.detail: The MDP state contains the noisy latent, noise level and condition. Its action is the next latent, not a robot command. Reward is terminal, after the future latent has been completed.

steps.name: Branch once, complete deterministically
steps.detail: Candidates share an initial noisy latent. Euler-Ancestral noise is injected at the first denoising transition; remaining transitions use Euler ODE updates. The Gaussian first transition supplies the likelihood ratio for policy optimization.

steps.name: Optimize and transfer
steps.detail: Compare completed candidates with the expert latent using negative L1 error plus cosine similarity. Normalize rewards within the group and maximize a clipped GRPO objective. Subsequently train the diffusion AGM on predictive features and demonstrated actions.

training.text: Simulation starts from VPP. CALVIN ABC contains 18,033 trajectories; a selected subset produces 129,454 clips. VPM post-training uses about 1,500 steps on 64 H20 GPUs, followed by roughly 10 AGM epochs on 8 H20 GPUs. Appendix A specifies ABC for AGM training; the main text says the whole CALVIN dataset.

Table S2 specifies group size 8, batch size 8, clipping 0.2, fine-tuning/post-training learning rates 10⁻⁴/10⁻⁶, and both reward weights 1.0. Table S1 lists 16-frame prediction, 256×256 images, a 10×7 action shape and 10 diffusion-transformer sampling steps.

inference.text: Extract multilayer VPM hidden states at the first denoising step and condition the separate DDIM-style action head on these features and language. Expert futures and GRPO scoring belong to training. Action-chunk execution frequency and replanning schedule are unspecified.

equations.explanation: Equation 16: x at noise level zero is the completed prediction; x₀ is the VAE-encoded expert future. The lambdas weight distance and directional agreement. Figure 2 instead draws positive L1 next to a plus sign; this explanation follows Equation 16.
Equation 17: candidate g is scored relative to its group of G rewards. No zero-standard-deviation safeguard is specified.

Equations 18–19: actions are sampled under the old policy. I indexes the first transition, rho is its new/old likelihood ratio, and epsilon-c sets clipping. Deterministic completion supplies the reward but no additional stochastic policy-ratio factors.

results.setting: Train on ABC; evaluate five-task chains in unseen D.
results.metric: Average completed trajectory length; five-task completion rate
results.comparison: VPP: 4.28; 74.7%. Updated VPM with original AGM: 4.35; 77.2%. Tri-VLA: 4.37; 81.8%.
results.interpretation: The VPP comparison gains 0.28 tasks and 8.4 percentage points. Most improvement accompanies subsequent AGM training; there is no AGM-only retraining control. Cross-family results do not establish matched compute.

results.metric: Average completed trajectory length; ten-task completion fraction
results.interpretation: Gains are 1.20 tasks and 0.11 absolute completion fraction. These ten-task results are separate from CALVIN percentages. Trial counts and uncertainty are not reported.

results.setting: CALVIN base versus post-trained VPM/AGM; Jacobian of actions with respect to visual features.
results.metric: Average effective rank; average normalized effective-rank ratio
results.interpretation: The paper uses squared sum of singular values divided by sum of their squares. Increased rank suggests broader visual sensitivity; it does not establish useful causal dependence.

results.task: CALVIN sampler, reward and optimizer ablations
results.setting: ABC→D, comparing each reported variant with the final configuration.
results.value: One-step SDE, latent reward and GRPO: 4.56
results.comparison: Five-step SDE: 4.34; pixel reward: 4.39; DDPO: 4.36; base: 4.28.
results.interpretation: Selected components outperform alternatives in these runs. Table S3 prints +0.08 for 4.39 versus 4.28, although the displayed difference is 0.11. Reward hacking remains an explanation, not a separately measured outcome.

results.setting: Apple grasp-and-place, bowl placement and dual-arm bottle placement; 200 demonstrations collected per task.
results.metric: Task score with partial credit; maximum 100 per Appendix B
results.value: Figure 5 shows higher VAMPO scores on all three tasks; exact scores are not printed.
results.comparison: Base VPP bars are lower in every panel.
results.interpretation: These are execution scores, not binary success percentages. Trial counts, error bars and aggregation details are absent. Bowl labels say box, whereas Appendix B describes placement onto a plate.

limitations.text: Latent agreement and decoded examples do not directly measure pose or contact accuracy. Figure 3 shows nonmonotonic loss; Figure S2 acknowledges imperfect texture and detail. The largest control gain changes both predictor and action-model training.

Table S5 gives average lengths 4.50, 4.31, 4.42 and 4.56 at 400, 600, 1,000 and 1,400 steps. Average length always exceeds the base here, but some 600-step short-chain rates fall below it. Repeated-seed uncertainty and checkpoint selection rules are absent.

Video comparisons span Agibot, Flexiv and a platform labeled VidowX; executed-task evidence is supplied for Agibot. Figure 5 labels wrist cameras RealSense 455, while Section 4.2 specifies D405. These are unresolved source discrepancies.

reproduction.text: Reproduction requires VPP initialization, the exact clip subset and preprocessing, reward reduction, noise schedule, old-policy refresh interval and gradient-detachment implementation. The PDF supplies architecture/hyperparameters but leaves these details incomplete; its code link alone establishes no reproducibility.

Proposed checks should pair first-step versus five-step stochasticity at matched budgets, and cross original/updated VPMs with original/retrained AGMs. Log latent error, task completion and uncertainty to separate reward improvement, transfer and extra action training. These are unexecuted proposals.

reasoning.text: Dual-system × IDM fits the explicit VPM-to-AGM architecture: future features condition a separate inverse-dynamics action generator. VAMPO post-trains prediction rather than jointly emitting future observations and actions from one model. Its reward operates during training, not inference-time search.

discussionQuestions: Does matched AGM-only retraining explain part of the gain attributed to predictive features?
Can latent reward improve while first-step features become less useful for control?
How sensitive are results to the chosen expert future when several futures are valid?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title/author/affiliation block and arXiv margin
evidence.detail: Title matches VAMPO: Policy Optimization for Improving Visual Dynamics in Video Action Models. The 19 authors match the catalog in order. The margin identifies arXiv:2603.19370v1 [cs.RO], 19 Mar 2026. Thirteen affiliations and code/model/project links are printed.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 2 and 4, Section 1 and Section 2.3
evidence.detail: Authors motivate post-training by a mismatch between likelihood surrogates and precise pose, contact and spatial-relation information needed for manipulation.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 3–4, Sections 2.1–2.2, Eqs. (1)–(6)
evidence.detail: Separate SVD-based VPM and diffusion AGM; expert video is VAE-encoded; first-step multilayer hidden states condition the AGM with language. Video and action denoisers use reconstruction objectives; the action head uses DDIM-style denoising.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, Eqs. (7)–(9)
evidence.detail: MDP state includes latent, noise level and condition; action is the next latent; terminal reward evaluates the completed output.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Sections 3.2–3.3, Eqs. (10)–(15)
evidence.detail: Euler-Ancestral sampling supplies a Gaussian transition. Hybrid sampling uses it only at the first transition and deterministic Euler updates thereafter, motivated by first-step feature relevance and credit assignment.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Algorithm 1 and Eqs. (16)–(19)
evidence.detail: Candidates share initial noise, complete hybrid rollouts, receive negative L1 plus cosine rewards against expert latents, and use group-normalized advantages. The clipped likelihood ratio indexes the first transition; old policy refresh is periodic without a stated interval.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Figure 2 and caption; p. 7, Eq. (16)
evidence.detail: Figure 2 shows conditioning, first-step SDE, ODE completion and latent comparison. Its positive mean L1 formula and plus sign omit the negative distance term in Eq. (16); mean versus norm reduction is also not reconciled.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Section 4.1, Simulation Settings and Training Details
evidence.detail: ABC→D uses an unseen environment; L-CALVIN extends chains from five to ten tasks. CALVIN ABC has 18,033 trajectories; a selected subset yields 129,454 clips. VPM uses about 1.5k steps on 64 H20 GPUs and AGM about ten epochs on eight H20 GPUs; evaluation uses RTX 5880.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Improvement in Action Execution and coupling paragraph; p. 9, effective-rank definition and Table 1
evidence.detail: Base / updated VPM with original AGM / updated VPM and AGM have lengths 4.28/4.35/4.56 and five-task rates 74.7/77.2/83.1. ER is (sum of singular values) squared divided by sum of squares. Base/full ER is 29.28/43.88 and ERR 0.0603/0.0814; middle-row coupling entries are missing.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Table 2, VPP, Tri-VLA and VAMPO rows; comparison paragraph
evidence.detail: VAMPO reports 98.0/94.8/91.3/88.3/83.1 and average 4.56; VPP 96.0/91.3/86.4/80.4/74.7 and 4.28; Tri-VLA 96.8/92.4/86.8/83.2/81.8 and 4.37. Authors state no extra network components or data are introduced.

evidence.location: PDF p. 10, Table 3, VPP and VAMPO rows, ten-task and Avg. Len columns
evidence.detail: L-CALVIN reports VPP ten-task fraction 0.28 and average 5.53, versus VAMPO 0.39 and 6.73. No repeated-run uncertainty is included.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Figure 3 and Analysis of Visual Dynamics
evidence.detail: Latent L1 loss decreases overall with fluctuations; qualitative panels compare expert, VAMPO and baseline under hallucination suppression, planning correction and action rectification labels. These are prediction comparisons.

evidence.location: PDF p. 10, Section 4.2, Real-World Settings and Training Details
evidence.detail: Execution platform is Agibot Genie 01; 14 arm DoF and 2-DoF gripper per end-effector are described. Three synchronized RGB-D views include D455 head and D405 wrist cameras. Each task has 200 demonstrations. Stages use 1.5k and 10k additional steps without a precise module mapping.

evidence.location: PDF p. 11, Figure 4 and caption; p. 10, Section 4.2
evidence.detail: Video panels identify Agibot, Flexiv and VidowX. L1 before/after values are respectively 0.2124/0.2014, 0.2694/0.2603 and 0.2304/0.2294. The body separates multi-embodiment video evaluation from Agibot execution.

evidence.location: PDF p. 11, Figure 5 and caption
evidence.detail: Setup, task examples and baseline/VAMPO score bars cover apple, bowl and two-bottle tasks. VAMPO bars are higher; exact labels, uncertainty and trial counts are absent. Head and wrist labels both say RealSense 455, conflicting with p. 10.

evidence.location: PDF p. 18, Appendix B, tasks (1)–(3) and Figure S1
evidence.detail: Apple and bowl tasks allocate 50 points to grasp and 50 to placement; bottles allocate 25 to each of two grasps and two placements. Maximum is 100. Bowl naming refers to a box, but the text describes a plate. Evaluation repetition and aggregation are unspecified.

evidence.location: PDF p. 17, Appendix A, Tables S1 and S2
evidence.detail: ABC is specified for both stages. S1 lists 16-frame video, 10×7 actions, 256×256 images, Video Former and diffusion-transformer configurations, and ten sampling steps for the latter. S2 lists G=8, batch=8, clipping=0.2, fine-tuning/post-training rates 10⁻⁴/10⁻⁶ and unit reward weights.

evidence.location: PDF p. 18, Appendix C, Table S3, Avg. Len column
evidence.detail: Base, pixel and latent rewards yield 4.28, 4.39 and 4.56. Printed pixel delta +0.08 conflicts with the displayed difference +0.11.

evidence.location: PDF p. 19, Table S4; p. 11, Hybrid Denoising Type
evidence.detail: Five-step SDE yields 4.34 and 76.4% five-task completion; first-step-only SDE 4.56 and 83.1%; base 4.28 and 74.7%. Reward hacking is the authors’ interpretation.

evidence.location: PDF p. 19, Table S5; pp. 10–11, Post-Training Steps
evidence.detail: Average lengths at 400/600/1000/1400 steps are 4.50/4.31/4.42/4.56. At 600 steps, one-/two-/three-task rates 95.6/90.6/85.6 are below base 96.0/91.3/86.4, despite higher average length.

evidence.location: PDF p. 19, Table S6; p. 11, Optimization Algorithm
evidence.detail: DDPO reaches average 4.36 and five-task rate 77.6; GRPO reaches 4.56 and 83.1. Authors hypothesize more stable updates but provide no variance measurement.

evidence.location: PDF p. 12, Figure 6 and caption
evidence.detail: Four panels compare 400/1400 steps, DDPO/GRPO, five/one SDE steps and pixel/latent reward. Success-rate and average-length bars use different vertical axes. Intermediate checkpoints appear only in Table S5.

evidence.location: PDF p. 20, Appendix D, Figure S2 and caption
evidence.detail: Two one-step prediction sequences compare ground truth, VAMPO and baseline. The caption acknowledges imperfect textures and detail while asserting improved motion dynamics.
